question: Francesca uses \(100\) grams of lemon juice, \(100\) grams of sugar, and \(400\) grams of water to make lemonade. There are \(25\) calories in \(100\) grams of lemon juice and \(386\) calories in \(100\) grams of sugar. Water contains no calories. How many calories are in \(200\) grams of her lemonade?
solution:
First find the mass and calories of the whole batch. Its mass is
\[
100+100+400=600\text{ grams}.
\]
The lemon juice contributes \(25\) calories, the sugar contributes \(386\), and the water contributes none, for a total of
\[
25+386=411\text{ calories}.
\]
For the same mixed lemonade, calories are proportional to serving mass. A \(200\)-gram serving is \(200/600=\tfrac13\) of the batch, so it contains
\[
411\cdot\frac13=\boxed{137}
\]
calories, choice B.

edges.reason: Contexts such as price, quantity and total, or speed, time and distance, supply familiar examples. Direct proportion can be learned through other contexts like side length and perimeter.
Direct proportion rests on a constant ratio value, which is ratio meaning. Proportion equations matter only when problems are solved by setting up a proportion.
